The second train leaves Dallas at 10am and travels at 80 mph. The distance between the two trains at 10am is 195 miles minus the 60 miles the first train has already traveled, which is 135 miles.

The relative speed at which the second train is closing the gap is the difference in their speeds:
\[ 80 \text{ mph} - 60 \text{ mph} = 20 \text{ mph} \]

The time \( t \) it takes for the second train to close the 135-mile gap is:
\[ t = \frac{135 \text{ miles}}{20 \text{ mph}} = 6.75 \text{ hours} \]

Since the second train leaves at 10am, they will meet 6.75 hours later:
\[ 10:00 \text{ am} + 6.75 \text{ hours} = 4:45 \text{ pm} \]

So, the two trains will meet at 4:45 pm.
